bodies.intuition: Byte-pair encoding builds a vocabulary by repetition. Start with single characters, count which adjacent pair occurs most often, merge it into one new symbol, and repeat. Common words fuse into single tokens; rare ones stay in pieces. The vocabulary is discovered from the corpus rather than chosen by anyone.
bodies.engineer: Run the merge loop until the vocabulary reaches its target size, then store the ordered merge list — applying it in the same order is what makes encoding deterministic. Operating on bytes rather than characters removes the unknown-token case entirely, since every input is representable. The frequency statistics come from the training corpus, so its composition is baked into the tokenizer.
bodies.math: Given a corpus of symbol sequences, repeatedly select the pair (a,b) maximising its count and replace all occurrences with a new symbol ab, for k iterations. The result is a vocabulary of size |Σ| + k and an ordered merge table applied greedily at encode time.

emphasis.intuition: discovered from the corpus rather than chosen by anyone
